projects.name: Nova Grants
projects.tagline: Grant intake, claim adjudication and funding oversight in Salesforce.
projects.summary: An independent, fictional Salesforce demonstration of the grant lifecycle: applicant intake, eligibility review, verified claims, reimbursement and executive reporting.
projects.seoDescription: Nova Grants is a fictional Salesforce grant-management demo with five-object data modelling, gated claim adjudication, funding safeguards and executive reporting.
projects.repoNote: Public repository reviewed on main. The README identifies the demo as independent and fictional.

cover.alt: Nova Grants executive dashboard with four Salesforce charts covering applications, claims, disbursements and capacity.
cover.caption: Executive dashboard from the demo org.

hero.alt: Nova Grants executive dashboard with four charts.
hero.caption: The coordinator view of the executive dashboard: applications, claims, disbursements and program capacity.

highlights.title: A five-object business model
highlights.body: Program, Application, Claim, Disbursement and Impact Metric sit around the standard Account, with claims and disbursements inheriting application access.

highlights.title: A real authorization gate
highlights.body: Adjudication requires a custom permission and actual Claim Edit access, not a System Administrator profile alone. Claims, applications and programs are locked during processing.

highlights.title: Financial logic with guardrails
highlights.body: Reimbursement is invoice amount × program percentage, rounded half-up and capped at the remaining approved amount. Unique payment references and repeat checks protect ordinary idempotency.

highlights.title: A mock ledger, labelled as one
highlights.body: A Queueable integration tracks Pending, Retrying, Failed and Synced states. No live general ledger is connected and no money is transferred.

evidence.label: Deployed tests passing
evidence.detail: Deployed automated regression, with 92% org-wide coverage including KPI rollup tests.

evidence.label: Components validated
evidence.detail: Standalone Metadata API validation without deployment; 34 test methods passed.

evidence.label: UAT reimbursement
evidence.detail: A $200 invoice at 50% produced one $100 disbursement, a Synced state and an idempotent repeat.

evidence.label: Reports and dashboard charts
evidence.detail: The owner verified all four reports and four charts, including coordinator folder access.

projects.evidenceNote: Results and UAT details are quoted from the repository's verified-status table. Browser evidence does not establish that both personas independently completed adjudication. Records are fictional.
limitations: Not an official Invest Nova Scotia or government implementation. Program parameters and records are fictional, and no money moves.
Agentforce is not implemented. A future-enhancement list is documented but not presented as completed functionality.
Direct application overcommitment and parallel-load behavior remain documented limitations in the architecture notes.
The advisement not to reset or re-adjudicate CLM-0006 for a presentation reflects the demo's recorded state, not a production workflow.

projects.name: Care Operations Analytics
projects.tagline: A funding, operations and risk dashboard for a fictional care provider.
projects.summary: A Python analytics pipeline and dashboard built on synthetic Canadian care data, from data-quality checks and a PostgreSQL-ready schema to Streamlit, Power BI and Tableau views.
projects.seoDescription: Care Operations Analytics is a synthetic-data Python project: 53 quality checks, a PostgreSQL-ready star schema, Streamlit, Power BI and Tableau dashboards and a claims-review risk model.
projects.repoNote: Public repository reviewed on main. All data and dashboards are explicitly synthetic.

cover.alt: The Care Portfolio Analytics Power BI dashboard with visit and completed-hour KPIs and service-type charts.
cover.caption: Care Portfolio Analytics in Power BI.

hero.alt: Power BI care portfolio dashboard with KPIs, a monthly trend and a service-type comparison.
hero.caption: Three reporting surfaces share one synthetic dataset. This is the Power BI care portfolio view.

highlights.title: Synthetic by design
highlights.body: The dataset covers 300 clients, 110 workers, 6 funders, 7,500+ service visits, 7,257 claims and 300 reconciliation exceptions, all generated for demonstration.

highlights.title: Validation before visualization
highlights.body: A 53-check data-quality layer separates valid records from invalid ones with audit logging, then produces processed CSV files for analysis.

highlights.title: Risk triage, not decisions
highlights.body: A logistic-regression score prioritizes claims for manual review. It is explicitly a triage aid and must not be used to approve, deny or determine care.

highlights.title: Three ways to see the work
highlights.body: A CSV-first Streamlit app needs no database; the same project also ships PostgreSQL-ready schemas and Power BI and Tableau dashboards.

evidence.label: Data-quality checks
evidence.detail: Reusable checks with invalid-record separation and audit logging.

evidence.label: Synthetic claims
evidence.detail: Across 7,500+ service visits, 300 clients, 110 workers and 6 funders.

evidence.label: Risk-model ROC-AUC
evidence.detail: Precision 0.632, recall 0.299 and F1 0.406 on the test set; modest by design on synthetic data.

evidence.label: Reporting surfaces
evidence.detail: Streamlit, a Power BI workbook and a Tableau executive dashboard.

projects.evidenceNote: Counts and model metrics are quoted from the project README and model documentation. They describe a synthetic dataset and are not business outcomes.
limitations: Every record is fictional and generated for portfolio demonstration. No real personal, healthcare, client, employee or company data is used.
The risk model is an interpretable prioritization aid, not an automated decision system. Its metrics are modest and reflect the limits of synthetic data.
Warehouse migration, dbt, Airflow/Prefect orchestration, role-based access, observability and production calibration are future work, not completed features.
No hosted deployment, authentication or live data connection is included.

projects.name: Gotcare Care Ledger
projects.tagline: A Salesforce funding ledger with auditable claim approvals.
projects.summary: A prototype for person-directed care funding: care plans, allocations, claims and ledger entries, with atomic Apex approvals and a balance alert that fires when funding crosses a threshold.
projects.seoDescription: Gotcare Care Ledger is a Salesforce prototype for person-directed care funding with atomic Apex claim approvals, ledger entries and a low-balance Flow.
projects.repoNote: Public repository reviewed on main. The project describes itself as a scratch-org prototype.

cover.alt: Typographic cover for the Gotcare Care Ledger.
cover.caption: Typographic cover. No screenshots are published.

highlights.title: Atomic approval path
highlights.body: approveClaim validates the claim, checks available funding, updates the allocation and plan, and inserts a ledger entry in one AuraEnabled transaction.

highlights.title: A lean data model
highlights.body: Care Plan → Funding Allocation → Care Claim / Ledger Entry, without an Opportunity or Quote dependency.

highlights.title: A deliberate alert
highlights.body: A record-triggered Flow emails only when a funding allocation crosses below 50% remaining, not on every edit while it stays below.

evidence.label: Custom objects
evidence.detail: Care Plan, Funding Allocation, Care Claim and Ledger Entry.

evidence.label: Claim approval
evidence.detail: All DML happens inside one Apex call, so a partial failure rolls back the approval.

evidence.label: Low-balance alert
evidence.detail: The Flow fires once when remaining allocation crosses below 50%.

projects.evidenceNote: Behaviour is described from the public repository documentation. No test counts or deployment receipts are claimed.
limitations: Scratch-org prototype: the org URL is ephemeral and must be recreated from the deployment instructions.
The low-balance email requires org-wide sender verification, deliverability settings and profile access; it is not a zero-configuration feature.
Amount meters are updated by the approval path; manual numeric edits are not automatically recomputed.
No screenshots are published, so this portfolio does not display any.
projects.galleryNote: No screenshots are published in the source repository.

projects.name: Agentic Job Search Workflow

projects.summary: Lane coverage, local posting checks, document-quality audits and CSV tracking, with dry-run defaults, explicit confirmation and dated backups before any write.
projects.seoDescription: A privacy-first Python CLI for local job-search operations: lane coverage, posting verification, document audits and CSV tracking with dry-run defaults and backups.
projects.repoNote: Public repository reviewed on main. The name is broader than the tool: it is deliberately not an auto-apply agent.

cover.alt: Typographic cover for the Agentic Job Search Workflow CLI.

highlights.title: Local by default
highlights.body: No network calls, scraping, browser automation or email sending. The tool operates only on local files and fictional sample data.

highlights.title: Writes need consent
highlights.body: Every write path previews first; persisting requires --no-dry-run --confirm and produces a dated backup before the original is replaced.

highlights.title: Operations, not applications
highlights.body: Lanes validate discovery coverage; verify checks posting links; docs audits visible artifacts; tracker manages a CSV application history.

evidence.label: Network calls

evidence.label: Default write mode
